questions.explanation: Candid means open and honest; 'frank' is the closest synonym.
Bene- means 'good' (as in benefit); benevolent means well-meaning and kind.
To mitigate is to make something less severe.
Tenacious describes someone who holds on firmly and does not give up.
Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation. Don't confuse it with 'ambitious'.
Lucid shares the root of 'lucent' (light); it means clear and easy to understand.
Austere means stern, plain, or severe in manner or appearance.
Prudent means showing good judgment and care for the future. 'Proud' is a sound-alike trap.
Ephemeral means lasting a very short time. 'Eternal' is its opposite.
Zealous means full of enthusiasm and energy for a cause.
Affluent: having a lot of money or possessions. Example: "The affluent suburb had large homes and private schools."
Amiable: pleasant and easy to get along with. Example: "The amiable instructor put nervous students at ease."
Arduous: requiring great effort; hard to do. Example: "The arduous march lasted twelve hours."
Audacious: willing to take daring risks. Example: "The audacious plan surprised everyone."
Belligerent: aggressive and eager to fight. Example: "The belligerent passenger was removed from the flight."
Brusque: short and rude in speech or manner. Example: "His brusque reply ended the conversation."
Cogent: clear, logical, and persuasive. Example: "She made a cogent argument for changing the schedule."
Copious: large in amount; abundant. Example: "He took copious notes during the lecture."
Cursory: quick and not thorough. Example: "A cursory inspection missed the cracked bolt."
Diligent: showing steady, careful effort. Example: "Diligent study before the test paid off."
Docile: easily led or controlled. Example: "The docile horse let the children ride it."
Erratic: irregular and inconsistent. Example: "The engine made an erratic noise before it quit."
Fastidious: very concerned with detail, accuracy, or cleanliness. Example: "The fastidious mechanic wiped every tool before putting it away."
Feasible: able to be done; practical. Example: "Landing on the short runway was feasible in calm wind."
Frugal: careful with money; avoiding waste. Example: "A frugal shopper, he always compared prices."
Gregarious: enjoying the company of others. Example: "The gregarious new pilot knew everyone's name by Friday."
Haughty: acting as if superior to others. Example: "The haughty officer ignored questions from junior staff."
Impartial: not favoring one side over another. Example: "An impartial judge reviewed the evidence."
Impetuous: acting quickly without thinking. Example: "His impetuous decision to take off in a storm was a mistake."
Incessant: continuing without stopping. Example: "The incessant alarm kept everyone awake."
Indolent: avoiding work or effort. Example: "The indolent student never finished his homework."
Inept: lacking skill or ability. Example: "The inept repair made the problem worse."
Jovial: good-humored and full of fun. Example: "The jovial crew chief joked with everyone."
Laconic: using very few words. Example: "Her laconic reply was simply 'Affirmative.'"
Lethargic: lacking energy; slow and drowsy. Example: "The heat left the whole squadron lethargic."
Meticulous: showing great attention to detail. Example: "Meticulous record-keeping is required for aircraft maintenance."
Mundane: dull and everyday; not exciting. Example: "Filing reports is a mundane but necessary task."
Nonchalant: calm and seemingly unconcerned. Example: "He was nonchalant about the delay, reading quietly at the gate."
Obsolete: no longer used or useful. Example: "The radar system was obsolete by the 1990s."
Ominous: suggesting that something bad will happen. Example: "Ominous clouds gathered over the runway."
Opulent: rich and showy; expensive-looking. Example: "The opulent hotel lobby had marble floors."
Placid: peaceful and not easily upset. Example: "The lake was placid at dawn."
Pragmatic: dealing with things in a realistic, sensible way. Example: "Her pragmatic solution fixed the problem with the tools on hand."
Precarious: not secure; dangerously likely to fall or fail. Example: "The ladder stood at a precarious angle."
Prolific: producing a great amount. Example: "The prolific author wrote three books a year."
Reticent: not revealing thoughts or feelings readily. Example: "He was reticent about his time overseas."
Robust: strong and healthy; able to withstand stress. Example: "The robust landing gear handled rough fields."
Sagacious: having good judgment and insight. Example: "The sagacious commander anticipated the problem."
Scrupulous: careful to do what is right and honest. Example: "A scrupulous accountant reported every error."
Serene: calm and untroubled. Example: "The serene countryside looked beautiful from above."
Sporadic: happening at irregular intervals. Example: "There was sporadic rain throughout the day."
Taciturn: saying little; habitually silent. Example: "The taciturn sergeant spoke only when necessary."
Trivial: of little value or importance. Example: "Don't waste time on trivial details."
Ubiquitous: seeming to be everywhere at once. Example: "Smartphones have become ubiquitous."
Vehement: showing strong feeling; intense. Example: "She made a vehement objection to the plan."
Verbose: using more words than needed. Example: "The verbose report could have been one page."
Volatile: liable to change suddenly and violently. Example: "Fuel vapor is highly volatile."
Wary: watchful and careful about possible danger. Example: "Pilots stay wary of wind shear near storms."
Adept: very good at something. Example: "She is adept at landing in crosswinds."
Astute: quick to notice and understand. Example: "An astute observer spotted the fuel leak."
Blatant: done openly and without shame; very obvious. Example: "It was a blatant violation of the rules."
Callous: showing no concern for others' feelings. Example: "His callous remark upset the family."
Capricious: changing mood or behavior suddenly. Example: "Mountain weather can be capricious."
Coherent: logical and consistent; easy to follow. Example: "Despite being tired, he gave a coherent report."
Deft: quick and skillful with the hands. Example: "With deft movements, she rewired the panel."
Dubious: not to be relied upon; suspicious. Example: "The source of the rumor was dubious."
Eloquent: fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing. Example: "The general gave an eloquent speech at graduation."
Fervent: showing intense feeling. Example: "He was a fervent supporter of the team."
Immaculate: perfectly clean and neat. Example: "Inspection required immaculate uniforms."
Lavish: generous or elaborate beyond what is needed. Example: "They threw a lavish party for the retirement."
Negligent: failing to take proper care. Example: "The negligent driver ran a red light."
Obstinate: refusing to change one's mind. Example: "The obstinate mule would not move."
Pensive: deep in thought, often seriously. Example: "She looked pensive as she studied the map."
Spurious: not genuine or valid. Example: "The report contained spurious data."
Tedious: long, slow, and dull. Example: "Counting inventory is tedious work."
Transient: lasting only a short time; passing. Example: "The turbulence was transient and soon passed."
Vigilant: alert and watching for danger. Example: "Guards remained vigilant all night."
Apathetic: showing no interest or concern. Example: "Voters were apathetic about the local election."
Benign: gentle; not harmful. Example: "The doctor said the growth was benign."
Cryptic: having a hidden or puzzling meaning. Example: "He left a cryptic note on the desk."
Futile: having no chance of success. Example: "Further searching in the dark was futile."
Lucrative: producing a lot of money. Example: "Airline pilots can have a lucrative career."
Meager: lacking in quantity or quality. Example: "They survived on meager rations."
Abate: to become less intense or widespread. Example: "We waited for the storm to abate."
Admonish: to warn or reprimand firmly. Example: "The instructor admonished the student for skipping the checklist."
Alleviate: to make suffering or a problem less severe. Example: "Medicine alleviated his headache."
Augment: to make larger by adding to. Example: "Extra tanks augment the aircraft's range."
Bolster: to support or make stronger. Example: "Good grades bolstered her application."
Coerce: to persuade by using threats or pressure. Example: "No one should be coerced into signing."
Condone: to accept or allow behavior that is wrong. Example: "The academy does not condone cheating."
Curtail: to cut short or limit. Example: "Bad weather curtailed flight training."
Deter: to prevent or discourage from acting. Example: "Bright lights deter birds from the runway."
Disparage: to speak about someone as having little value. Example: "He disparaged his rival's work."
Elicit: to draw out a response or reaction. Example: "The question elicited a long silence."
Embellish: to add details to make more attractive, sometimes untrue. Example: "He embellished the story to make it more exciting."
Emulate: to copy someone in an effort to match them. Example: "Young pilots emulate their instructors."
Exacerbate: to make a problem worse. Example: "Fatigue exacerbates poor decision-making."
Expedite: to make something happen faster. Example: "The clerk expedited the paperwork."
Fabricate: to make up something false; or to build. Example: "He fabricated an excuse for being late."
Hinder: to get in the way of; slow down. Example: "Heavy snow hindered the rescue."
Impede: to delay or prevent by getting in the way. Example: "Fallen trees impeded traffic."
Implore: to ask urgently and emotionally. Example: "She implored him to reconsider."
Instigate: to bring about or start something, often trouble. Example: "He instigated the argument."
Jeopardize: to put at risk. Example: "Skipping maintenance jeopardizes safety."
Lament: to express grief or regret. Example: "The town lamented the loss of its factory."
Mollify: to calm someone's anger or anxiety. Example: "An apology mollified the angry customer."
Negate: to cancel the effect of. Example: "The headwind negated the faster engine."
Procrastinate: to put off doing something. Example: "Don't procrastinate on studying for the AFOQT."
Rectify: to fix or make right. Example: "The error was rectified the next day."
Relinquish: to give up willingly. Example: "The captain relinquished command to his replacement."
Reprimand: to scold formally. Example: "The officer was reprimanded for being late."
Scrutinize: to inspect closely and carefully. Example: "Inspectors scrutinized every weld."
Substantiate: to provide evidence to support a claim. Example: "Can you substantiate your claim with data?"
Supplant: to take the place of. Example: "Jets supplanted propeller aircraft on long routes."
Thwart: to prevent someone from accomplishing something. Example: "Security thwarted the break-in."
Undermine: to gradually damage or weaken. Example: "Rumors undermined trust in the leader."
Vindicate: to clear of blame or prove right. Example: "The investigation vindicated the pilot."
Waver: to be unsure or unsteady. Example: "She did not waver in her decision."
Ascertain: to find out for certain. Example: "The crew tried to ascertain the cause of the noise."
Concur: to have the same opinion. Example: "The doctors concurred on the diagnosis."
Corroborate: to support with evidence. Example: "Two witnesses corroborated his story."
Deplete: to use up the supply of. Example: "The long flight depleted the fuel reserves."
Discern: to notice or recognize something hard to see. Example: "He could barely discern the runway lights through the fog."
Enhance: to increase in quality or value. Example: "New software enhanced the radar's accuracy."
Feign: to fake a feeling or condition. Example: "He feigned illness to skip the run."
Forfeit: to give up as a penalty. Example: "The team forfeited the game by not showing up."
Adversary: an enemy or opponent. Example: "Know your adversary's strengths."
Anomaly: something that differs from what is normal. Example: "The sensor reading was an anomaly."
Aptitude: a natural ability to do something. Example: "The AFOQT measures aptitude for different careers."
Benefactor: a person who gives help, especially money. Example: "An anonymous benefactor funded the scholarship."
Candor: the quality of being open and honest. Example: "I appreciate your candor about the problem."
Catalyst: something that causes an important change. Example: "The accident was a catalyst for new safety rules."
Consensus: general agreement among a group. Example: "The committee reached a consensus."
Deference: polite submission to someone's opinion or authority. Example: "Out of deference to the general, everyone stood."
Dilemma: a situation requiring a difficult choice. Example: "Divert or continue? It was a real dilemma."
Facade: an outward appearance that hides something. Example: "His calm was only a facade."
Fallacy: a mistaken belief or faulty reasoning. Example: "It is a fallacy that heavier planes always fly slower."
Fortitude: strength of mind in facing pain or danger. Example: "She showed great fortitude during recovery."
Hierarchy: a system of levels of authority. Example: "The military has a clear hierarchy."
Impetus: a force that makes something happen. Example: "The new law gave impetus to the project."
Integrity: being honest and having strong moral principles. Example: "Integrity first is an Air Force core value."
Malice: the desire to harm others. Example: "He acted out of malice, not ignorance."
Novice: a person new to an activity. Example: "As a novice, he practiced landings daily."
Paradox: a statement that seems self-contradictory but may be true. Example: "It's a paradox that slowing down can get you there sooner."
Proximity: closeness in space or time. Example: "The base's proximity to the city was convenient."
Rapport: a friendly, understanding relationship. Example: "Good rapport between crew members improves safety."
Remorse: deep regret for a wrong committed. Example: "He felt remorse for his mistake."
Respite: a short period of rest or relief. Example: "The holiday gave a brief respite from training."
Valor: great courage in the face of danger. Example: "The pilot received a medal for valor."
Zenith: the highest point. Example: "At the zenith of her career, she commanded a wing."
Vigor: physical strength and good health. Example: "He attacked the problem with vigor."
Apathy: lack of interest or concern. Example: "Apathy among members led to poor attendance."
Compliance: the act of following rules or requests. Example: "Compliance with safety rules is mandatory."
Discrepancy: a difference between things that should match. Example: "There was a discrepancy between the two fuel gauges."
Acumen: skill in making good judgments quickly. Example: "Her business acumen made the company profitable."
Camaraderie: trust and friendship among people who spend time together. Example: "The camaraderie of the squadron lasted for decades."
Deluge: a severe flood or an overwhelming amount. Example: "A deluge of applications arrived after the announcement."
Fervor: intense and passionate feeling. Example: "They cheered with fervor."
Nuance: a slight difference in meaning or expression. Example: "Good translators understand every nuance."
Prerogative: a right that belongs to a particular person or group. Example: "It is the commander's prerogative to cancel the mission."
Squalor: a state of being extremely dirty and unpleasant. Example: "The refugees lived in squalor."
Abundant: existing in large quantities. Example: "Water was abundant after the spring rains."
Acute: severe or intense; also keen and perceptive. Example: "She has an acute sense of hearing."
Adamant: refusing to change one's mind. Example: "He was adamant that the checklist be followed."
Agile: able to move quickly and easily. Example: "The agile fighter jet turned sharply."
Aloof: cool and not friendly; keeping apart. Example: "The new officer seemed aloof at first."
Ample: enough or more than enough. Example: "There was ample time to finish the test."
Arbitrary: based on chance or whim rather than reason. Example: "The rule seemed arbitrary to the cadets."
Articulate: able to express ideas clearly. Example: "She gave an articulate answer to the board."
Brazen: bold and without shame. Example: "It was a brazen attempt to cheat."
Cordial: warm and friendly. Example: "The two commanders had a cordial meeting."
Credible: able to be believed; convincing. Example: "The witness gave a credible account."
Dauntless: showing courage and determination. Example: "The dauntless crew flew into the storm to rescue survivors."
Despondent: in low spirits from loss of hope. Example: "After failing twice, he felt despondent."
Discreet: careful in what one says or does to avoid offense. Example: "Please be discreet about the new assignment."
Elusive: difficult to find, catch, or achieve. Example: "The answer remained elusive."
Exemplary: serving as a desirable example. Example: "Her exemplary record earned her a promotion."
Exuberant: full of energy and excitement. Example: "The exuberant graduates threw their caps."
Formidable: inspiring fear or respect through size or strength. Example: "The obstacle course was formidable."
Frivolous: not having any serious purpose or value. Example: "Don't waste money on frivolous purchases."
Genial: friendly and cheerful. Example: "The genial host greeted every guest."
Hostile: showing opposition or dislike; aggressive. Example: "The pilots flew over hostile territory."
Innate: existing from birth; natural. Example: "She had an innate talent for navigation."
Intrepid: not afraid of danger. Example: "The intrepid explorer crossed the ice cap."
Lenient: not strict in punishing or judging. Example: "The lenient instructor allowed a retake."
Mediocre: only ordinary; not very good. Example: "His first landing was mediocre."
Nebulous: unclear or not well defined. Example: "The plan was too nebulous to act on."
Prominent: important or easily seen. Example: "A prominent general spoke at graduation."
Resilient: able to recover quickly from difficulty. Example: "Resilient airmen bounce back from setbacks."
Stoic: enduring pain or hardship without complaint. Example: "He remained stoic through the long march."
Tangible: able to be touched; real. Example: "The training produced tangible results."
Tenuous: very weak or slight. Example: "His connection to the case was tenuous."
Unanimous: fully in agreement. Example: "The vote was unanimous."
Venerable: respected because of age or wisdom. Example: "The venerable aircraft flew for fifty years."
Vivid: producing strong, clear images; intense. Example: "He gave a vivid description of the crash."
Abhor: to hate strongly. Example: "She abhors dishonesty."
Acquiesce: to accept something without protest. Example: "He acquiesced to the new schedule."
Advocate: to publicly recommend or support. Example: "The report advocates more simulator time."
Allocate: to distribute for a particular purpose. Example: "The base allocated funds for new radios."
Ameliorate: to make something bad better. Example: "New lighting ameliorated night conditions on the ramp."
Berate: to criticize angrily. Example: "The coach berated the team after the loss."
Circumvent: to find a way around an obstacle or rule. Example: "They circumvented the traffic by taking back roads."
Deviate: to depart from an established course. Example: "The pilot deviated around the thunderstorm."
Diminish: to make or become less. Example: "The noise diminished as the jet climbed away."
Emanate: to come out from a source. Example: "Heat emanated from the engine."
Endorse: to declare public approval of. Example: "The commander endorsed the proposal."
Eradicate: to destroy completely. Example: "The program aimed to eradicate the disease."
Exonerate: to clear from blame. Example: "The board exonerated the pilot."
Fortify: to strengthen, especially against attack. Example: "Engineers fortified the bunker."
Hamper: to slow or prevent progress. Example: "Fog hampered the search."
Incite: to encourage or provoke action. Example: "The speech incited a riot."
Insinuate: to suggest something indirectly. Example: "He insinuated that she had cheated."
Mandate: to officially order. Example: "The rules mandate a preflight briefing."
Placate: to make less angry. Example: "The manager placated the upset traveler."
Refute: to prove a statement wrong. Example: "The data refuted his theory."
Reiterate: to say again for emphasis. Example: "The instructor reiterated the safety rules."
Rescind: to cancel officially. Example: "The order was rescinded the next day."
Adherence: the act of following rules closely. Example: "Strict adherence to procedures prevents accidents."
Ambivalence: mixed feelings about something. Example: "She felt ambivalence about moving overseas."
Ardor: great energy and passion. Example: "He studied with ardor."
Brevity: the use of few words; shortness. Example: "Radio calls require brevity."
Calamity: an event causing great damage. Example: "The flood was a calamity for the town."
Conjecture: an opinion formed without proof. Example: "The cause of the crash was only conjecture."
Diligence: careful and persistent effort. Example: "Her diligence paid off on the test."
Eminence: fame or importance in a field. Example: "A scientist of great eminence spoke."
Feat: an act of skill or courage. Example: "Landing without power was an amazing feat."
Humility: a modest view of one's own importance. Example: "Good leaders show humility."
Lethargy: a lack of energy. Example: "Heat brought on lethargy."
Magnitude: great size or importance. Example: "They underestimated the magnitude of the storm."
Obscurity: the state of being unknown or unclear. Example: "The author died in obscurity."
Prudence: good judgment in practical matters. Example: "Prudence dictated a diversion to another airport."
Tenacity: the quality of not giving up. Example: "Her tenacity got her through pilot training."
Vestige: a small remaining part of something. Example: "Not a vestige of the old runway remained."
